blocks.title: Testing and Recovery Exercises exam shortcuts
items: Discuss roles without changing production → TABLETOP
Participants walk through the response verbally.
Example: Teams discuss actions during a ransomware scenario.
Actually switch to alternate system/site → FAILOVER
The organization tests whether the backup can take over.
Example: Production traffic moves to the DR environment.
The exercise imitates an event to test response.
Example: Staff respond to a simulated data-center outage.
Run primary and backup simultaneously → PARALLEL PROCESSING
Both systems process work so results can be compared.
Example: A recovery system runs alongside the current one.
blocks.example: Focus on recovery speed, continuity, redundancy, data loss tolerance, and site or power requirements.

questions.q: Participants discuss how they would respond to a ransomware incident without changing production systems. Which test is this?
questions.explanation: A tabletop is a discussion-based walkthrough.

questions.q: Production traffic is intentionally switched to the disaster recovery environment to verify takeover works. Which test is this?
questions.explanation: Failover testing verifies the alternate environment can take over.

questions.q: Employees respond to a realistic but controlled mock data-center outage. Which exercise best fits?
questions.explanation: A simulation imitates a real event for practice.

questions.q: The primary and recovery systems run at the same time and their results are compared. Which testing approach is this?
questions.explanation: Parallel processing runs both environments simultaneously.
